evidence: Phrases La Rock is credited with originating at Herc's parties, including the hotel-motel construction, appear in 'Rapper's Delight' without any credit to him. The attribution rests on Bronx oral history rather than on a document, which is why this sits at consensus, and it is also exactly why no credit was ever assigned: an unrecorded phrase circulating in a scene has no paperwork behind it.

earlier.title: shout-outs over Herc's records at Bronx parties

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen to 'Rapper's Delight' for how much of it is stock phrasing rather than anything written for the record. The hotel-motel lines, the call-and-response, the way the rappers hand off to each other: none of that was invented in a studio in New Jersey in 1979. It was the common language of Bronx parties, being recorded for the first time by people who mostly were not the ones who built it.

explanation.age7: Some of the words on the first rap hit came from parties years earlier, and the people who made them up got nothing.
explanation.age13: By 1979 there was a shared stock of phrases that MCs in the Bronx all used, some of which La Rock is credited with starting. When Sugar Hill made 'Rapper's Delight', that language went onto the record, and the credit and the money went to the people who recorded it. Nobody stole anything in a legal sense. There was simply no way for a phrase shouted at a park jam in 1975 to belong to anyone.
explanation.adult: This edge is about the collision between an oral, communal form and an industry built on fixed authorship. Held at consensus deliberately, because the attribution is oral history and the same unrecordability is the substance of the claim. It pairs with the Chic interpolation on the same record, where the uncredited party had lawyers and was added to the credits, and the uncredited party without lawyers was not.
